langs.title: A website and tools in 9 languages
langs.text: Every tool follows the chosen language: the keyboard, the instructions and the exercises. Arabic is written right to left, Hindi in Devanagari, and Chinese in pinyin with tones.
story.title: Classroom materials, on the computer and tablet
story.text: DISSIPL is a group of special education teachers. Our tools recreate the hands-on materials we use every day with students who have special educational needs. In our experience, they help every student.
story.t1: For students: learn differently, at their own pace
story.t2: For teachers: a resource to project and use in groups
story.t3: For parents: understand school exercises better
story.alt1: Two children using an abacus in class
story.alt2: Wooden Montessori moveable alphabet, red consonants and blue vowels
story.alt3: Montessori number cards and golden beads
method.title: Learning starts with the hands
method.text: An approach rooted in active learning, with the child at the center.
method.s1.title: Handle
method.s1.text: Students move beads, letters, cards or pieces, just like with classroom materials.
method.s2.title: Understand
method.s2.text: They see what numbers, sounds and fractions represent, without being rushed.
method.s3.title: Practice
method.s3.text: Premium exercises follow curriculum skills, level by level.

voices.title: What students and teachers say
q1: The digital abacus helps me understand numbers better, because in normal lessons I can't always follow when my teacher talks.
q2: This website is really useful for my grade 6 students who struggle, especially in math. The digital abacus turns out to be a powerful tool.
q3: Math is a bit hard for me. But when I do it on the computer and have fun, it's great!
q4: My students have cognitive disorders, sometimes severe, and some of them manage to work on Dissipl with enthusiasm.
q5: I like using the app because it's like games, but for learning.
q6: I constantly have to adapt teaching materials to make learning easier. Dissipl helps me a lot.
r6: Coordinator of an inclusive education unit
q7: Sometimes our teacher uses the digital abacus. She puts it on the board, we discuss in groups and then we correct the problems.
q8: What a great idea to have active learning tools like Montessori, but online! I use Dissipl alongside the physical materials.
q9: I'm good at math. But I like using DISSIPL, especially for the interactive exercises.
q10: Some of my grade 6 students need to go back over the basics, and Dissipl helps them a lot.
q11: When we go to the computer room to use the website, we're never bored. I learn better this way.
q13: I like going on DISSIPL because it lets me work differently.
faq.title: Have a question?
faq.text: Write to us at contact@dissipl.fr or read the full FAQ.
faq.a1: Hands-on learning online. Our tools recreate real teaching materials that we use every day with students who have special educational needs.
faq.a2: Every tool has a free version for hands-on exploring. The full versions, with built-in exercises by skill level, are for Premium subscribers.
faq.a3: The tools are designed for students with dyslexia, dyscalculia, ADHD or cognitive disorders. In our teaching experience, every student can use them.
faq.a4: The website and the tools are available in 9 languages: French, English, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Hindi and Chinese. Choose yours at the top of the page.
